**User testing — what visitors did** — the analytics re
ads, and the model pass\nover them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are\ndeterministic and free; the insights

request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and
feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which
models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sig
nals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` |
Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One w
indow's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **
No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |\n|
`DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |\n| `POST .../studie
s/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regener

ate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response includes an `analysis`
summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session\ncoverage. Failure/skip
reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog
\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map independently. Reading this response neve

r starts analysis.

Taxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme ids
remain stable across additions
and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired or replaced\nmembers
hip remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version provenance, not historical traffic

snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-scope total. Map reads separa
tely expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover only its requested\ngoa

l runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather
than a fabricated map node.

The five analytics shapes ab
ove are documented as **open objects** on purpose.\nTheir upstream projections grow with the product and the SDK types them the\ns

ame way, so pinning a field list would turn every new metric into a spec
violation. Read what you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It still draws on the same `insig
htsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the window read rather\n> than

re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is
> why it is never inferred from anything else.

**Feed

back** — report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST /feedback` | S
end a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summary, details?, operation?, req
uestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-in accounts only (guests get
`401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated strictly — an empty or over-long ke
y is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text goes to the MCPJam team, outside your

organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool
calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one —\n> it lets the team find that request in th
e server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` with the original\n> receipt instead

of filing a second report.

**Planning** — one read that answers "may I?" before you try:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| -
| - |\n| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, the beta gate's state, plan limits, and the booleans to

branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write still enforces
> independently, so
a `true` here that races a flag flip costs you a clean\n> `403` rather than an incorrect success — and nothing should consult it\n
> *instead of* trying. It exists because agent surfaces are static: an MCP tool\n> catalog is built with no organization in hand,
so the alternative is\n> attempting the write and reading the failure, by which point the agent has\n> usually already told someon

e what it was about to do.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCPJa

m/inspector/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)
for Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## Server accounts

A saved ser
ver signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users\ncan't use the browser sign-in, for example because a password an

d a passkey
are required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token
to a named account before each run.
\
n| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../accounts` | The accounts you
can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | O
ne account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`,
same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: true`), or both |\n| `DELETE .
../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"
}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\
n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensi
tive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformation\": { \"clientId\": \"'\"$CLIENT_I

esAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an account

`{account}` is an acc
ount id or a name. A well-formed account id is always\nread as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`, and an upload to a
n\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account has makes `PUT` create the acc

ount; on every other route it
answers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A
name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and\nis at most 64 characters. One outside that rule, o
r one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are\nunique on the server, ignoring c

ase.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, and
 replacing a tok
en replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name\n for one test user.\n* **Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted
runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner\n included. Asking for it
is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** The body\n takes onl
y `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token

` is
 refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.
* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**
* **A refresh token
